newsitem.title: FRANCE: No proof gelatine from BSE cows is safe - expert.
newsitem.headline: No proof gelatine from BSE cows is safe - expert.

text.p: The former director of the Central Pharmacy of Paris Hospitals said on Tuesday there was no way of checking for certain that products containing gelatine from cattle infected with mad cow disease were safe to use.

"Recognising a product is free of BSE is suspect because we haven't got the means to ensure there is no transmission (to humans)," Eric Poster told a European Parliament committee of inquiry into Bovine Spongiform Encephalopathy (BSE) or mad cow disease.
European Union scientists continue to discuss whether new heat processing rules are adequate to eradicate mad cow disease from gelatine.

This follows a report received by Farm Commissioner Franz Fischler on June 25 which criticised rules approved by the Commission on June 11 saying beef by-products could be used if heated to 138 to 140 degrees centigrade for four seconds.
Poster said he did not approve of the World Health Organisation's (WHO) attitude, which he described as "waiting around until an exponential phase of the epidemic to take a decision".

His comments came after Dr Meslin of the WHO told the committee of inquiry that WHO recommendations on human health protection were based on the suspicion that BSE was transmissible to people but that there was no definitive, scientific proof that this was the case.
Poster said the situation reminded him of the early eighties, when most people ruled out the possibility of an AIDS epidemic.
